items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I got Steve Grossman and David Liebman, and Gene Perla.

ctx.x: Okay so let’s go back to, again, Jimmy Garrison is having some personal problems, which preclude him from continuing on in the Elvin Jones Trio. Who did you get to replace him?

Gene Clark, and after that Joe was, he was a little bit… He was doing a lot of record dates and all that so I got Steve Grossman and David Liebman, and Gene Perla. I still didn’t have a pianist (Laughs).

I’m holding in my hand a copy of “Poly Curtains” and this date is September 26th, a little after your birthday of that year in 1969 and this one has a composition entitled “Mr. Jones” this one has Joe Farrell and also George Coleman and Wilbur Little on bass and Condita on congas. This happened to be a particular favorite of mine. I just wanted to ask Keiko about “Mr. Jones” since that happen to be one of my favorites.

items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Parents lived in the same building with Max Roach and Elvin Jones... He was my conduit to knowledge.

ctx.x: Yeah. I would imagine. All right. So that’s your first experience with Coltrane. Obviously that was a life-shifting experience for you.

Eventually. Certainly not that night, although I tell it like it was. Epiphanies don’t happen immediately. They take time to enlarge and magnify and get exaggerated with time, because we exaggerate. But it certainly made me – the main thing is, it made me see, this is not a hobby. What can I say? I’m still 15 years old. This is not just playing saxophone in school band. That’s the same instrument I have at home in Brooklyn under my bed. This can’t be possible, that’s the same instrument. It’s a tenor saxophone.…
When you were in high school, did you have a band director who was especially hip to these things?
